walkthroughs.body_html:
Specialist Technical Principles — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Specialist Technical Principles brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Specialist Technical Principles.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why are ribs moulded into plastic products?
options: To increase stiffness without adding much weight
To make the product heavier
To trap air for insulation
Purely for decoration

mcqs.q: Why do designers use standard components such as screws and hinges?
options: They are cheaper and more reliable than making custom equivalents
They make products harder to repair
They are required on every product by law
They eliminate the need for quality control

mcqs.q: Which scale of production runs 24 hours a day making one product, such as paper?
options: Continuous production
One-off production
Batch production
Prototype production

mcqs.q: What is the difference between hardness and toughness?
options: Toughness measures how well a material resists rusting.
A hard material is automatically a tough material.
Hardness is resistance to scratching and indentation; toughness is the ability to absorb impact without fracturing. Hard materials are often brittle rather than tough.
Tension only occurs in metal components.

mcqs.q: Why are ribs added to plastic mouldings?
options: They increase stiffness and strength using very little extra material, keeping the moulding thin, light and quick to produce.
Ribs are added to make the plastic easier to melt down for recycling.
Toughness measures how well a material resists rusting.
Ribs are added purely as decoration on the hidden side of products.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between tension and compression?
options: Toughness measures how well a material resists rusting.
Tension is a pulling force that stretches a material; compression is a pushing force that squashes it. A bent beam experiences both at once on opposite faces.
Tension and compression are the same force given different names in different materials.
Tension only occurs in metal components.
